hints.content:
A reflection moves a point perpendicularly across a line, so that the [[☃ definition 1]] is the same distance from the line as the [[☃ definition 2]], but on the other side.



[[☃ image 1]]

This means that the line of reflection is the line that contains the midpoints between corresponding points of the pre-image and image.

options.definition: The figure *after* one or more transformations

options.alt: Point R is reflected across a line to form point R prime. Segment R R prime is perpendicular to the line.

hints.content:
We could pick any pairs of corresponding points to help us find the line of reflection. 

First, let's find the midpoint between $\blueD{A(-1,3)}$ and $\maroonD{A'(1,5)}$.

$\left( \dfrac{\blueD{-1}+\maroonD{1}}{2}, \dfrac{\blueD{3}+\maroonD{5}}{2}\right)=(0,4)$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Quadrilateral ABCD and Quadrilateral A prime B prime C prime D prime are drawn. Quadrilateral ABCD has point A at negative one, three, point B at negative one, negative one, point C at zero, negative three, and point D at three, zero. Quadrilateral A prime, B prime, C prime, and D prime with point A prime at one, five, point B prime at five, five, point C prime at seven, four, and point D prime at four, one. There is a plotted point at zero, four at the endpoint of one line segment connected to A and another line segment connected to A prime. These line segments are congruent.

hints.content:
We could find the line that passes through $(0,4)$ and is perpendicular to the segment $\overline{AA'}$, or we could find a second midpoint.

Let's find the midpoint between $\blueD{B(-1,-1)}$ and $\maroonD{B'(5,5)}$.

$\left( \dfrac{\blueD{-1}+\maroonD{5}}{2}, \dfrac{\blueD{-1}+\maroonD{5}}{2}\right)=(2,2)$



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. Quadrilateral ABCD and Quadrilateral A prime B prime C prime D prime are drawn. Quadrilateral ABCD has point A at negative one, three, point B at negative one, negative one, point C at zero, negative three, and point D at three, zero. Quadrilateral A prime, B prime, C prime, and D prime with point A prime at one, five, point B prime at five, five, point C prime at seven, four, and point D prime at four, one. There is a plotted point at two, two at the endpoint of one line segment connected to B and another line segment connected to B prime. These line segments are congruent.

hints.content:
The line shown here passes through both midpoints and is perpendicular to $\overline{AA'}$ and $\overline{BB'}$. So it is the line of reflection.



[[☃ image 1]]

Quadrilateral ABCD has point A at negative one, three, point B at negative one, negative one, point C at zero, negative three, and point D at three, zero. Quadrilateral A prime, B prime, C prime, and D prime with point A prime at one, five, point B prime at five, five, point C prime at seven, four, and point D prime at four, one. There is another plotted point at zero, four at the endpoint of one line segment connected to A and another line segment connected to A prime. These line segments are congruent. A line passes through both plotted points.
